distinguishing_features: Uses an ion-exchange layer that binds/sequesters chloride ions rather than dosing a molybdate inhibitor that raises pitting potential
Relies on a passive surface treatment (deposited coating) rather than active scheduled chemical injection via pumps/DCS
Targets reduction of local electrolyte chloride activity/conductivity instead of shifting E_pit upward
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent chloride ions from accumulating at and attacking electrical contact points in a high-salinity environment, so that contact corrosion (and resulting VSWR drift) is mitigated.
parsed.viable_reason: An ion-exchange sacrificial layer that sequesters chloride is a physically plausible passive-treatment mechanism and the VSWR/conductivity coastal-exposure test is executable as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Neither the closest art's scheduled inhibitor dosing nor passive barrier coatings capture the idea of a chloride-binding ion-exchange surface layer, so the distinguishing mechanism is not a routine parameter change of the prior art.
